gloss: to rush in; to run into

definitions.gloss: to rush in; to run into
definitions.explanation: To run quickly into a place, often in a hurry or to seek refuge.
To hurry to meet a deadline, often at the last minute.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきたので、{店|みせ}に{駆|か}け{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: It started raining, so I rushed into the store.

examples.japanese: {発車|はっしゃ}{直前|ちょくぜん}の{電車|でんしゃ}に{駆|か}け{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To rush onto a train just before departure.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りに{駆|か}け{込|こ}みで{間|ま}に{合|あ}った。
examples.english: I made it by rushing just before the deadline.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
{駆|か}ける (to run, to gallop) + {込|こ}む (into)

TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive) - takes に for the destination

RELATED NOUN:
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}み: last-minute rush
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}み{乗車|じょうしゃ}: rushing onto a train (discouraged by station announcements)
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}み{寺|でら}: refuge temple (historically for women seeking divorce)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}みセーフ: just barely making it
- {駆|か}け{込|こ}み{需要|じゅよう}: last-minute demand (before a deadline or price increase)
